note: The fleet's only CONTRADICTING signal. Every case below pins one distinct outcome or reason; the three `unknown` reasons are pinned separately because a supervisor acts on the REASON, and the no-git rows exist to prove the port never turns 'I could not check' into 'you lied'.

cases.note: the whole reason this exists: three files claimed, git shows none — the one alert that can contradict an agent

SAME claim, git absent instead of empty: unknown/no-git, NEVER mismatch. A folder workspace has no git to ask, and an absent answer is not a discrepancy — crying mismatch here trains a supervisor to ignore the alert
an empty array is a REAL git answer ('nothing changed') and must not collapse into null — contrast with the row above
the claim is true
missing (claimed but absent — alarming) and unclaimed (changed but unclaimed — sloppy) are DIFFERENT lists, reported at once and never merged
unclaimed alone is still a mismatch: a worker that touched a file it never mentioned is sloppy, not lying, but the supervisor still needs the row
unknown/not-completed: a running task has not said anything yet, so there is nothing to contradict
precedence: status is read BEFORE the result, so a running task with garbage in `result` is not-completed ('wait'), not unreadable-result ('go read the row')
unknown/unreadable-result: `result` is not JSON at all
unknown/unreadable-result: no result row at all is 'nothing was written', not 'claimed nothing'
unknown/unreadable-result: valid JSON of the wrong TYPE — a bare string is not an object
unknown/unreadable-result: a write cut off mid-flush (crashed worker) is unreadable, and must not read as a claim of the files it managed to emit
precedence: the result is parsed BEFORE git availability is checked, so an unreadable result on a folder workspace names the row, not the workspace
normalization: the two sides spell the same file differently — ./a and a are one file
normalization: leading and trailing slashes are shape, not identity
normalization: surrounding whitespace AND a U+FEFF byte-order mark are trimmed — JS trims ZWNBSP where Rust's char::is_whitespace does not, so a naive port invents a mismatch here
the other direction of the same trap: U+0085 (NEL) IS Unicode White_Space, so Rust's trim would eat it, but JS keeps it — the port must keep it too and report the mismatch TS reports
normalization does NOT touch backslashes: a Windows-spelled claim reads as missing against git's posix answer. Pinned as the current shared behaviour of both sides, not as an endorsement
the CLAIM keeps its duplicates: one file named twice stays two entries, so the count stays the worker's own arithmetic and the double-naming is visible
git's side is a Set: de-duplicated, and `unclaimed` reports it in FIRST-occurrence order
non-string entries in filesModified are dropped, not coerced: a claim is only as good as the parts of it that are paths
entries that normalize to nothing are dropped rather than compared as the empty path
a JSON ARRAY is `typeof 'object'` in JS, so it parses as a claim of nothing rather than as unreadable — a serde-shaped port that demanded a map would report the wrong REASON here
an object with no filesModified key is a claim of nothing, not an unreadable result: older result shapes omitted the field entirely
filesModified present but the wrong TYPE degrades to 'claimed nothing' rather than to unreadable
drops non-string entries and reports completedBy as null when it is absent
extra keys the several result shapes have carried are ignored, not rejected
a non-string completedBy is null, not a coerced number — the field names a worker or nothing
not JSON at all
valid JSON, wrong type
JSON null is not an object — the `parsed === null` arm, which typeof alone would miss
no result row
an empty result column is the falsy arm, not a parse attempt
the summary for no-git NEVER says mismatch — the sentence a supervisor reads is the whole point of degrading to unknown
cases.expected: cannot check on a folder workspace

cases.note: not-completed and unreadable-result share one phrase, and it is not an accusation either
the same phrase for an unreadable result: the console distinguishes them by REASON, not by sentence
when both directions are non-empty the ALARMING one wins the sentence
cases.expected: claimed 2 file(s) git does not show as changed

cases.note: sloppy-only reads as sloppy, not as a false claim
cases.expected: changed 1 file(s) it did not claim

cases.note: a match counts the CLAIM, duplicates included — the number is what the worker said, not a file count

exactly ONE leading ./ is stripped — the TS replace has no /g, so a doubled prefix survives and the claim legitimately fails to match. Uncovered before: de-globbing the port's strip_prefix was the one mutation the corpus did not kill
duplicate JSON keys: the LAST filesModified wins, as JSON.parse and serde_json both resolve it — a reconciler that rewrote the row mid-flush must not read the stale key
the claim keeps duplicates on the ALARMING side too: one file named twice with git showing nothing reports missing twice, so the count stays the worker's own arithmetic

a BOM before the DOCUMENT is a parse failure on both sides — contrast with the BOM inside a path above, which is trimmed. JSON.parse and serde_json agree here, and the port must not 'helpfully' skip it
a WELL-FORMED surrogate pair (an emoji in a filename) survives both readers intact — the contrast case for the lone-surrogate divergence below
nesting well under serde_json's 128-frame recursion limit still reads on both sides — the green boundary for the depth divergence below
NFC and NFD are DIFFERENT paths: neither side unicode-normalizes, so a macOS-decomposed git path never matches a precomposed claim. Pinned so no one 'fixes' it in one language only

cases.allowDivergence: PORT BUG, UNFIXED — serde_json stops at 128 nested frames and JSON.parse does not, so a result carrying a deeper trace reads as a claim in the shipping TS and as unreadable-result in the Rust port. Recorded, not blessed: the fix is a design call about the serde_json dependency, see the module note
cases.note: DIVERGENCE: nesting deeper than serde_json's recursion limit. TS reports match; the port reports unknown/unreadable-result

cases.allowDivergence: PORT BUG, UNFIXED — and the worst of the three, because it silences a REAL alert: TS reports mismatch on this row and the port reports unknown. serde_json rejects an unpaired surrogate escape that JSON.parse accepts (a JS string is UTF-16 and can hold one; a Rust String cannot), so one bad code unit anywhere in the result turns a contradiction into 'I could not check'
cases.note: DIVERGENCE: lone surrogate escape in a claimed path. TS reports mismatch; the port reports unknown/unreadable-result

cases.allowDivergence: PORT BUG, UNFIXED — serde_json rejects a numeric literal that overflows f64 ('number out of range') where JSON.parse yields Infinity and reads on. The number is in a field this decision never looks at, and it still costs the whole verdict
cases.note: DIVERGENCE: a number literal that overflows f64, in a field the claim ignores. TS reports match; the port reports unknown/unreadable-result
